L162: ## Reviews
L163:

L170: ## About This Game
L171: 
L172: Prepare for the deepest, most intricate simulation of a world that has ever been created.
L173: 
L174: 【65†Image†shared.fastly.steamstatic.com】
L175: 
L176:   * Not just generated geometry -- a whole simulated world. Generated rise and fall of civilizations, personalities, creatures, cultures, etc. Infinite hours of gameplay.
L177: 
L178:   * Now with beautiful pixel graphics!
L179: 
L180:   * Learn the basics with in-game tutorials
L181: 
L182:   * A lifetime “living” project - created/updated since 2003, with no end in sight
L183:   * Generate your unique world and manage a bustling colony of dwarves, even as they probably mine towards their eventual demise.
L184: 
L185:   * A new endless hobby, just for you!
L186: 
L187: 【66†Image†shared.fastly.steamstatic.com】
L188: 
L189: The legendary Dwarf Fortress is now on Steam! Build a fortress and try to help your dwarves survive, despite threats of starvation, dragons, and madness.
L190: 
L191: 【67†Image†shared.fastly.steamstatic.com】
L192: In this complex construction/management/roguelike simulation, every generated world brings a unique challenge, whether it’s dwarves with their own simulated personalities or aquifers. Observe what makes your civilization fall into eventual decline, and learn for next time… until something else inevitably goes wrong.
L193: 
L194: The combat model includes skills, body parts, material properties, aimed attacks, wrestling, pain, nausea, various poison effects, and much more.
L195: It’s difficult to convey the depth of the generation. Hundreds of animals and monsters, many of which are randomly created for each world, as well as generated poetry, musical forms, instruments, and dances for your dwarves to practice and perform. A dynamic weather model tracks wind, humidity, and air masses to create fronts, clouds, storms, and blizzards. Over two hundred rock and mineral types can appear, in their proper geological environments.
L196: 
L197: Remember: Losing is fun!
L198: 【68†Image†shared.fastly.steamstatic.com】
L199: 
L200: This is still good old Dwarf Fortress, but with graphics support and music provided. A few bells and whistles won’t change its essence.
L201: 
L202: Classic Dwarf Fortress mod-artist Jacob "Ironhand" Bowman collaborated with artists Carolyn Jong and Neoriceisgood to create an all-new sprite pack for the game, which they continue to add to regularly.
L203: Dwarf Fortress also has hours of music in a two-volume soundtrack by Dabu and Simon Swerwer, including tracks in the Dwarvish language!
L204: 
L205: It's never been easier to start playing! We've improved the new player experience with the addition of tutorials to guide you through building your first fort and keeping your dwarves happy.
L206: 
L207: 【69†Image†shared.fastly.steamstatic.com】
L208: Command your dwarves as they search for wealth in their generated mountain. Your dwarves will need a steady supply of food and beer, but they’ll also need your guidance in surviving attacks from hostile civilizations, the wilderness, or even the dead.
L209: 
L210:   * Craft treasures and furnitures from various materials
L211: 
L212:   * Establish a barony and support the increasingly demanding nobility
L213: 
L214:   * Read your dwarves’ thoughts to keep them happy
L215:   * Build floodgates to divert water for farming, and/or prevent magma mishaps
L216: 
L217:   * Build structures and watch your dwarves discover and build their culture, like taverns, libraries, temples, honey, wax, pottery, animal training, bookbinding, and more.
L218: 【70†Image†shared.fastly.steamstatic.com】
L219: 
L220:   * Go anywhere! Explore any civilization, earn a reputation, and recruit followers to join you
L221: 
L222:   * Experience your fortress and the simulation in a new, more embodied way
L223:   * Explore mythical dungeons to find magical items, artifacts, and fill your quest journal
L224: 
L225:   * Hints of mythology and magic as a start of future simulation enrichment to come
L226: 
L227:   * An additional hour of music from Dabu and Simon Swerwer, presented as a second volume of the original soundtrack
L228: 
L229: 【71†Image†shared.fastly.steamstatic.com】
L230: 
L231:   * The original inspiration for RimWorld, Prison Architect, Minecraft and more.
L232: 
L233:   * One of the first video games acquired by the Museum of Modern Art in New York
L234:   * Updated for over 16 years by two brothers, Tarn “Toady One” and Zach “Threetoe” Adams, and with the support of Kitfox Games since 2020.
L235: ## Mature Content Description
L236: 
L237: The developers describe the content like this:
L238: 
L239: Dwarf Fortress contains textual descriptions of violence, and static 2D sprites that may have violent ends. Alcohol consumption is required for a dwarven fortress to run smoothly, as described in text. Dwarves can experience mental anguish, and in extreme cases this can lead to them taking their own lives or the lives of others.
